`charport` is a small interoperability layer for ALTREP character vectors. It
lets backend packages keep strings in their own storage while consumer packages
read those strings through one common byte-view interface.

The package has three pieces:

1. A C ABI for resolving any character vector into a `charport_reader`.
2. C++ convenience wrappers in `charport.h`, especially `charport::Reader`.
3. `charvec`, a reference ALTREP string class with serial and sharded builders.

The ABI is pre-release. Downstream packages should call `charport::check_abi()` at
load time and expect recompilation when the ABI version changes.

## Performance snapshot

The current benchmark uses the enwik8 corpus split into 1.13 million strings
(94 MB of string data). It compares the ordinary `STRING_ELT` / `SET_STRING_ELT`
paths with `charport::Reader` and the `charvec` builders. The read benchmark
explicitly registers `charvec` as a reference backend; normal package load
leaves the backend registry empty until backend packages opt in.

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("bench.png")
```

## R helpers

The R API is small:

```{r}
library(charport)

x <- charvec("alpha", "beta", NA)
typeof(x)
is_charvec(x)
as.character(x)
```

Diagnostics expose the currently registered backends and the backend serving a
specific vector:

```{r}
charport_backends()
charport_backend_of(x)
```

`charvec` is a storage class. It preserves the bytes and encoding marks it is
given; it does not translate strings to UTF-8 or reject non-UTF-8 input.
It is not registered with the broker on package load; backend packages register
their own ALTREP classes explicitly.

## Reading in C++

Consumer packages add `LinkingTo: charport` and `Imports: charport`, include
`charport.h`, and resolve a reader on the main R thread:

```cpp
#include "charport.h"

extern "C" SEXP C_total_bytes(SEXP x) {
  charport::Reader r(x);
  double total = 0;
  for(charport::StrView s : r) {
    if(!s.is_na()) total += s.len;
  }
  return Rf_ScalarReal(total);
}
```

`charport::StrView` is a borrowed view: `ptr`, byte `len`, and `enc`. `ptr == NULL`
means `NA`. The bytes are not NUL-terminated by contract.

A reader borrows the vector. While the reader or any view is in use, keep the
vector protected and do not access or mutate it through the R API, including
through aliases. The ALTREP class controls materialization and mutation, which
may invalidate backend storage.

For threaded consumers, resolve on the main R thread and only copy the raw
reader to workers when `reader.reentrant()` is true.

## Building a `charvec`

The serial builder is for single-threaded construction:

```cpp
charport::charvec::Builder b(n);
for(R_xlen_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
  b.set(i, bytes, len, charport_enc::CE_UTF8);
}
SEXP out = b.to_charvec();
```

When output bytes are produced directly, `reserve()` avoids an intermediate
buffer:

```cpp
char * dst = b.reserve(i, len, charport_enc::CE_UTF8);
std::memcpy(dst, src, len);
```

For parallel construction, use `charport::charvec::BuilderMT`. Each worker gets a
distinct shard index and a disjoint element range. Workers fill their shards
without calling the R API; `to_charvec()` runs on the main thread after all
workers join.

## Backend registration

A backend package registers an ALTREP class at load time:

```cpp
static void * my_init(SEXP x) {
  return R_ExternalPtrAddr(R_altrep_data1(x));
}

static charport_strview my_get(void * state, R_xlen_t i) {
  const my_store * s = static_cast<const my_store *>(state);
  return make_strview(s->ptr(i), s->len(i), charport_enc::CE_UTF8);
}

charport::register_backend(my_class, my_init, my_get, true);
```

`my_init()` runs once per resolved vector on the main R thread. `my_get()` runs
per element and must not call the R API or throw C++ exceptions across the ABI.
If `reentrant = true`, `my_get()` must also be safe to call concurrently.

See `vignette("developer-guide", package = "charport")` for the full contract.
